source_metadata.title: Large Language Models as Clinical Support Tools in Drug Information Services: Performance Comparison With Pharmacists
source_metadata.journal: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy
source_metadata.source_type: research report; comparative evaluation of LLM responses to real-world drug information questions

issues.description: The DOCX supplement belongs to the same publication and supplies Tables S1 and S2. It was not treated as a separate study.
Model and platform labels are preserved as reported by the article. No external verification of those labels was used to rewrite source facts.
Pharmacist-provided DIC responses were the reference standard only for concordance. The source does not establish them as an independently adjudicated clinical truth standard.

extraction_limitations: Atoms remain review_status=needs_review because this run did not include human verification.
Table 7 multi-metric citation-error profiles are preserved as qualitative_result row atoms because the current QuantitativeResult object represents one effect measure per atom.
The 102 individual questions in Supporting Table S2 were inspected as the benchmark dataset but were not atomized one by one because they are inputs, not study findings.
Bibliography entries were extracted to Markdown and were not treated as evidence atoms.
